title: Embedding and Freezing Fresh Human Tissue in OCT Using Isopentane
author: Kenny Roberts
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.95mh846

steps.title: Fix tissue in formalin
steps.instruction: Transfer tissue to 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin (e.g., CellStor Pot) and fix at 4 °C or at room temperature for 2–36 hours, depending on tissue type and downstream application.

steps.title: Cryoprotect with sucrose
steps.instruction: Prepare a 30 % (w/v) sucrose solution using sterile de‑ionised water. Move the tissue directly from formalin into the sucrose solution and incubate at 4 °C overnight; tissue will initially float and sink once sucrose permeation is complete, indicating successful cryoprotection. Do not cryoprotect non‑fixed tissues.

steps.title: Prepare isopentane‑dry ice slurry
steps.instruction: Place a small metal box on dry ice, fill it with isopentane to a depth of several centimetres, and slowly add dry ice while stirring to minimise violent boiling. Continue adding dry ice until the mixture reaches approximately –78 °C (monitor with a thermometer); further dry ice will not cause strong bubbling. Keep the box in an insulated container on a down‑flow table to limit exposure to CO₂, isopentane vapour, and aerosols. The slurry is ready when bubbling is minimal.

steps.title: Label and pre‑fill cryomoulds with OCT
steps.instruction: Label each cryomould with sample ID and at least one orientation axis (e.g., dorsoventral, anteroposterior). Fill the moulds with OCT medium and let them sit for several minutes to minimise bubble formation.

steps.title: Pre‑chill PBS and set up ice dishes
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill ~20 mL of sterile PBS (or HBSS) on ice. Fill a disposable 150 mm Petri dish with ice and place a smaller 30–60 mm dish on top; add the chilled PBS to the smaller dish.

steps.title: Rinse tissue and examine under microscope
steps.instruction: Process tissues one at a time. Rinse each tissue in the pre‑chilled PBS on ice, then examine it with a dissection microscope to assess anatomical context before embedding.

steps.title: Trim tissue if needed
steps.instruction: If required, use a disposable scalpel to trim or dissect the tissue to obtain desired pieces, specific regions, or to separate tissues that were shipped together.

steps.title: Pick up tissue and remove excess buffer
steps.instruction: Using a perforated Moria spoon, gently pick up the tissue. Wick away excess PBS with blotting filter paper without allowing the tissue to contact the paper directly; either dab surrounding droplets with a paper corner or place the spoon on filter paper and let liquid seep through the perforations. Handle delicate (e.g., fetal) tissue carefully to avoid damage.

steps.title: Embed tissue in OCT and orient
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue into the pre‑filled OCT cryomould using a spoon or spatula. If residual buffer streaks are visible, gently stir the OCT with forceps or a small spoon to remove them. Adjust the tissue orientation as desired; if the tissue floats, gently push it to the bottom of the mould. Optionally photograph or sketch the orientation and update the mould markings.

steps.title: Freeze cryomould in isopentane slurry
steps.instruction: Using a pair of forceps, place the cryomould level into the isopentane‑dry ice slurry, keeping it level to prevent loss of OCT or sample movement. Hold the mould immersed at the top of the liquid until the OCT begins to freeze; avoid early flooding of the OCT surface to prevent bubbles. Freeze for about 5 minutes for tissues ≤ 500 mm³ (time may vary with size). If the tissue protrudes after the bottom freezes, add additional OCT to cover it, ensuring isopentane does not flood the frozen surface.

steps.title: Remove frozen mould and drain isopentane
steps.instruction: When the OCT is completely solid, lift the cryomould out of the slurry onto fresh dry ice to allow residual isopentane to drain and evaporate. The mould may be kept on dry ice while other samples are processed.

steps.title: Wrap mould in foil and label
steps.instruction: Wrap each frozen cryomould individually in aluminium foil, label the foil with sample ID, date, and orientation, and minimise the time the sample spends away from dry ice to reduce temperature change.

steps.title: Store samples at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the foil‑wrapped moulds to a pre‑cooled cryobox and store at –80 °C.
